about: Memory database by type (from SMBIOS). The CPU entry adds the platform's sweet-spot speed.

families.name: DDR5
tips: Turn on XMP (Intel) or EXPO (AMD) in the BIOS: DDR5 runs at 4800-5600 without it.
First boot after enabling it can show a black screen for 1-3 minutes while memory trains: that is normal.
Two sticks run faster and more reliably than four.
On AM5, 'Memory Context Restore' shortens later boot times.
issues: Four DDR5 sticks often cannot reach the kit's rated speed: lower it one step if the PC will not boot.

families.name: DDR4
tips: Turn on XMP / DOCP / A-XMP: DDR4 runs at 2133-2666 without it.
Two sticks in slots A2 + B2 (see the board manual) for dual channel.
AMD Ryzen: keep FCLK at half the RAM speed (1800 for DDR4-3600).

families.name: DDR3
tips: Enable XMP if the board offers it; DDR3 systems gain most from dual channel.
issues: DDR3 platforms are too old for Windows 11 support.
